newsitem.title: UK: AMEC sees sustained profit recovery in '97.
newsitem.headline: AMEC sees sustained profit recovery in '97.

text.p: British engineering and construction group AMEC Plc said on Wednesday it expected its profit recovery to be sustained in 1997, boosted by an improved trading environment for its businesses.

"In the United Kingdom in particular, the market at long last is now moving in our favour, not least because we have, over the years, been moving AMEC away from the traditional form of adversarial contracting into the new world of partnership and alliances," chairman Sir Alan Cockshaw said in a statement from AMEC's annual meeting.
However, he added that the company's German building and civil engineering business continued to incur trading losses due to that country's depressed market conditions.

"Fortunately, the momentum of our profit recovery should be sustained in 1997 by the significant improvement in the performance of our housing business and paybacks from our recent investments," he said.
Cockshaw will retire next month and be succeeded by Sydney Gillibrand. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
